title: The Job Interview
setup: You're interviewing for a role you want. The interviewer is professional but hard to read, giving little away.
openingLine: Thanks for coming in. So, walk me through why you're looking to leave your current role.

npcTurns.text: That's fair. A lot of people underestimate how much team dynamics affect day-to-day satisfaction. What's the biggest thing you'd want to be different here?
Good, that lines up with how we operate. Tell me about a time something you were working on went wrong. What happened?
I appreciate the honesty there, a lot of candidates dodge that question entirely. We move fast here, sometimes messily. How do you handle ambiguity?
Understood. Compensation-wise, what range are you targeting for this move?
Noted, that's within reason for the level we're hiring at. Do you have any questions for me before we wrap up?

title: Asking for a Raise
setup: You've scheduled time with your manager to discuss compensation after a year of expanded responsibilities. She's supportive but budget-conscious.
openingLine: So you wanted to talk about your role — what's on your mind?

npcTurns.text: You're right that your scope has grown a lot this year. I want to be upfront that budget is tight right now. What number were you thinking?
That's higher than I can approve outright, but let me push on it. Can you send me a summary of the specific projects that justify it?
Good. Even if the full number doesn't clear this cycle, is there anything else — title, flexibility, a bonus — that would matter to you?
That's reasonable, I can advocate for that piece even if the base salary takes longer. What's your timeline expectation on hearing back?

title: The Roommate Confrontation
setup: Your roommate has repeatedly left dishes and shared bills unpaid for weeks. You've decided to finally bring it up directly.
openingLine: Hey, do you have a few minutes? I wanted to talk about how things have been around the apartment.

npcTurns.text: Okay... I mean, I know the dishes have piled up a bit. Is this about that?
Fair, I didn't realize the electric bill was still sitting there too. I've just been slammed at work, it's not intentional.
I hear you. What would actually make this easier for you going forward — a schedule, reminders, something else?
That sounds doable. I'll get the bill sorted tonight. Are we good?

title: Comforting a Grieving Friend
setup: Your close friend's father passed away last week. You've come over to sit with them for the evening.
openingLine: Thanks for coming. I don't really know what I'm supposed to say to people right now.

npcTurns.text: It's weird, some moments I'm fine and then it just hits me out of nowhere. Is that normal?
I keep thinking about the last conversation we had. It wasn't even about anything important, just small talk.
Everyone keeps telling me he's in a better place. I don't know if that actually helps me, honestly.
Can you just stay a bit longer? I don't want advice, I just don't want the house to feel this empty right now.

title: Meeting the In-Laws for the First Time
setup: You're having dinner at your partner's parents' house for the first time. Her father is friendly but clearly evaluating you.
openingLine: So, my daughter says you two have been together almost a year now. How'd you two actually meet?

npcTurns.text: Interesting, small world. What do you do for work these days?
Good, stable field. My daughter mentioned you're close with your family too — do you all get together often?
That's good to hear, family matters a lot around here. Where do you two see things heading, if you don't mind me asking?
Fair enough, no need to rush an answer at the dinner table. Glad you're here — pass the potatoes?

title: The Customer Service Complaint Call
setup: You're calling to dispute a billing error on your account. The representative sounds tired but is trying to be helpful.
openingLine: Thanks for calling in, I see you're disputing a charge — can you walk me through what happened?

npcTurns.text: I understand the frustration, that's definitely not supposed to happen. Let me pull up your account — can you confirm the date of the charge?
Got it, I see the duplicate charge now. I can refund it, but it'll take three to five business days to post. Is that workable?
Great, I've submitted that now. Is there anything else on the account you wanted me to look at while I have it open?
Perfect, you'll get a confirmation email shortly. Anything else I can help with today?

title: Mediating Two Arguing Friends
setup: Two of your close friends had a falling out over a canceled trip and both came to you separately. Now they're in the same room, and it's tense.
openingLine: I don't even know why we're doing this. She's the one who bailed on the trip with two days' notice.

npcTurns.text: Oh, so now it's my fault my mom got sick? Unbelievable.
I did tell her, the day I found out. She's acting like I sat on it for a week.
Fine — what exactly do you think I should've done differently, given my mom was in the hospital?
...Okay, that's actually fair, the deposit thing wasn't really about the cancellation itself. I think I was just scared and took it out on you.
I don't want to keep fighting about this. Can we just agree to actually talk to each other next time instead of going quiet?

title: The Awkward Reunion With an Ex
setup: You unexpectedly run into an ex at a mutual friend's wedding. You haven't spoken in two years since the breakup.
openingLine: Oh — wow, hi. I didn't know you'd be here. You look... good. This is weird, huh?

npcTurns.text: Yeah, it has been a while. I've actually been doing okay, mostly. How about you, still at the same job?
Good, glad to hear it. I wasn't sure how tonight would go, running into you like this.
Honestly, for what it's worth, I've thought about reaching out a few times, just to say there's no hard feelings on my end.
That actually means a lot to hear. Are we... okay? Like, can we be normal around each other tonight?

title: Requesting Feedback on Your Toast
setup: You're giving a best man's toast at your brother's wedding in two days and asked a trusted friend to review a draft with you.
openingLine: Okay, I read through it twice. Overall it's good, but can I be honest with you about a couple parts?

npcTurns.text: The opening story is great, but the middle section drags — it's like three separate stories mashed together. Which one matters most to you?
Okay, that one's the strongest, cut the other two down to a sentence each. How are you planning to land the ending?
That ending will actually get people. One more thing — how nervous are you about delivering this live?
That's normal, everyone is. Want to run through it out loud with me right now once more?

title: Negotiating the Price of a Used Car
setup: You're trying to buy a used car from a private seller. He's listed it slightly above what comparable ones are going for.
openingLine: So, I've had a lot of interest in this one already. What did you want to offer?

npcTurns.text: That's a bit lower than I was hoping for. What makes you land on that number specifically?
Fair, I hadn't seen those other listings. I could come down some, but not all the way there. What if we met closer to the middle?
I can do that if you're paying cash today and taking it as-is, no additional inspection contingency. Deal?
Great, let's get the paperwork sorted then. Do you want to handle the transfer today or tomorrow?

title: The Tense Talk With Your Teenager
setup: Your sixteen-year-old has been coming home past curfew and shutting down whenever you bring it up. You're trying again tonight, differently this time.
openingLine: I don't want this to turn into a fight. Can we just talk about the last couple weekends for a minute?

npcTurns.text: Here we go again. It's not a big deal, I'm just hanging out with my friends.
...Fine. Honestly some nights I just don't want to come home yet, it's loud here with you and dad lately.
I didn't think you even noticed that stuff. Is that actually why you've been staying out later?
Okay. I don't have a fix for the loud part tonight, but can we agree on a text-by-eleven thing instead of a hard curfew?

title: Reconnecting With an Old Friend
setup: You're grabbing coffee with a friend you haven't seen in five years, since before you both moved to different cities.
openingLine: This feels so overdue. I honestly wasn't sure what to expect walking in here today.

npcTurns.text: Same, honestly. A lot's changed — I got divorced last year, actually. Feels strange saying it out loud still.
It's been a rough stretch, but I'm coming out the other side of it now, I think. What about you, how's life been treating you?
That's great to hear, genuinely. I always wondered if we'd drift for good once we both moved.
Can we actually make this a regular thing again, even just twice a year? I don't want another five years to slip by.
